Each is a single line in which the two end nodes have one neighbor and every inner node has two." width="100%"} Creates a sequence of `n` nodes connected linearly: `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> ... -> n`. End nodes have degree `1`, internal nodes have degree 2. A path graph (often written P_n) has `n` nodes and `n - 1` edges, is connected, and contains no cycles, so it is the simplest possible tree. Its diameter is `n - 1`, the largest of any connected graph with `n` nodes. That makes it a handy test case and building block: - checking algorithms against known answers (shortest paths, diameter, centrality) - modelling linear structures like pipelines, supply chains, or sequences of events - adding a "tail" or chain onto another structure Each node is labelled with its own node ID as a string: in an empty graph they are `"1"` to `"n"`, and if the graph already has 3 nodes they are `"4"` to `"n + 3"`. In a directed graph the edges point from each node to the next. The path is added as a new, separate component; it isn't connected to any existing nodes. The graph is modified in place, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step in the step log (see `steps`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the path. Must be at least `1` (a single node with no edges); the path will have `n - 1` edges. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node type/category assigned to all new nodes (stored in the `type` column of the node DataFrame). Default is `None`, which leaves the type unset. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), label each node with its ID as described above, so labels match IDs even after nodes have been deleted. If one of those labels is already used in the graph, a `ValueError` is raised before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional relationship label assigned to all edges of the path (stored in the `rel` column of the edge DataFrame). Default is `None`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A path graph connects `n` nodes end-to-end in a single line, so it always has one fewer edge than it has nodes: ::: {#8397a289 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(n=5) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (5, 4) ``` ::: ::: The two end nodes have degree `1` and every inner node has degree `2`, and the distance between the ends is the longest possible for five nodes: ::: {#0667c754 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node_df()["degree"].to_list(), graph.diameter() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ([1, 2, 2, 2, 1], 4) ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph each edge points to the next node. `type=` and `rel=` tag the nodes and edges, which suits a linear process such as a train line: ::: {#fa9a088f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} line = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_path_graph(n=4, type="station", rel="track") line.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Calling it again adds a second, disconnected path whose labels continue the numbering: ::: {#47c70d58 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(n=3).add_path_graph(n=3) graph.get_node_df()["label"].to_list(), graph.count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` (['1', '2', '3', '4', '5', '6'], 2) ``` ::: :::
